claims.head: Carlsson gets company tonight
claims.call: The Islanders’ L2 (Heineman, Pageau and Duclair) spends at least 39% of its 5-on-5 time against the Ducks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Islanders keep sending Pageau’s line (Heineman, Pageau and Duclair) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter DeBoer has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Ducks’ first line is Killorn, Carlsson and Klepov.

claims.head: The Ducks kill penalties far better than the Islanders
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but the Islanders are one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Islanders more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 8 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mathew Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matias Maccelli is out 4-6 weeks (lower body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 37% last season.

NYI.head: The Islanders have a slight edge
NYI.body: Anaheim is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Terry, while the Islanders have home-ice advantage. Then again, Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, and the Islanders will be without Barzal. Still, it’s close: the Ducks can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.
